page.layout: One printed page, cut in half; this part shows its upper portion. Centred from top to bottom: a small printed ornament "(○)" in parentheses, then a woodcut headpiece of foliage and grotesque figures, then the title in capitals with a small italic "De", and a last title line. Faint show-through of mirrored text from the reverse lies at the top and along the right edge and is not transcribed.; One text block of full lines with a large woodcut initial P at the upper left; running head "Thesis I." at the top above the text; signature "A 2" at the foot, catchword "hoc" at the right below the last line.

page.notes: The woodcut headpiece has a large decorated letter A within foliage, with human and animal figures. The "De" is in a smaller italic script. The printed ornament above the headpiece is a circle in parentheses. The lower part of the page is not on this image. The first word is a woodcut initial P joined to "hilosophiæ"; the printed reading is "Philosophiæ". The opening line is partly under the initial and the transcription of the first letter is uncertain. Greek phrase "τὸ Θεῖον" is copied as best read.
